title: Activating the "Minimize All" widget should close open Panel popups, as the "Peek at Desktop" one does
line: Clicking Minimize All Windows now also closes an open Kickoff or System Tray popup, like Peek at Desktop does.
explanation: Peek at Desktop goes through KWin's show-desktop mode, which activates the desktop, so popups that hide on focus loss close. Minimize All only asks the task manager to minimize each window and never moves focus, so an open Kickoff or System Tray popup stayed on screen over the empty desktop. The applet now walks every applet in the shell (including the System Tray's own applets) and collapses those whose popup is open and would hide on focus loss; pinned popups stay open, as with Peek.

commits.message:
applets/showdesktop: close applet popups when minimizing all windows

Minimize All only minimized windows and never moved focus, so an open
Kickoff or System Tray popup stayed on top of the desktop, unlike with
Peek at Desktop. It now also closes popups that hide on focus loss.

BUG: 481615

media.caption: Master: Kickoff open (top), then Minimize All Windows clicked (bottom): Konsole is minimized but Kickoff stays open.
With the fix: same steps, Kickoff closes together with the windows.
Master: System Tray's Power & Battery popup stays open after Minimize All Windows.
With the fix: the tray popup closes too.

review.text: The cause is right: Minimize All never moves focus, so focus-loss popups stay open. But an applet walking every containment and applet in the Corona and collapsing their popups is a layering workaround that maintainers are unlikely to want in a single applet. The fix is also knowingly incomplete: the System Tray's own expanded view still stays open because of a missing binding in plasma-workspace, which the brief says should be patched too.
changes: Add the plasma-workspace systemtray change that binds the tray's hideOnWindowDeactivate to its pin setting, so the tray's hidden-items view also closes.

Move 'collapse all unpinned applet popups' out of the showdesktop applet into the shell/libplasma (e.g. a Corona or ShellCorona call the applet invokes), instead of the applet iterating the whole Corona itself.
